abstract: This record is the five-part Landscape/Atlas and audit-trail series for a multi-route investigation toward the Riemann Hypothesis. It documents foundations, obstruction analysis, route failures, computer-assisted diagnostics, spectral route design, and cross-route synthesis. The record is a conditional reduction and research atlas, not an unconditional proof of the Riemann Hypothesis. Cite this record for the full landscape, audit trail, excluded strategies, supporting certificates, and historical development of the programme. For focused companion records, see EvenDom v1.9 and Zookeeper v1.5 under Related records below. PAPERS IN CURRENT v3.1 RECORD Part I: Foundations and Obstructions (English, 15 pages; German, 15 pages). Part II: Even Dominance / Branch A (English, 55 pages; German, 56 pages). Part III: Spectral Routes / Branches B and Z (English, 13 pages; German, 14 pages). Part IV: Cross-Route Synthesis (English, 9 pages; German, 9 pages). abstract: We prove strict log-concavity of the Riemann-Jacobi kernel, establish hyperbolicity of the Jensen polynomials J_{d,n}(x) for d &lt;= 22, n &lt;= 14, and prove that the global Riemann Hypothesis is algebraically equivalent to a subluminal condition on the Wronskian components. Part I (Sections 2-5) proves the kernel is strictly log-concave (TP_2) with curvature kappa &gt;= 19.24, via the convex potential decomposition and a perturbation bound using only 4.3% of the log-concavity budget. Part II (Sections 6-8) establishes K_{d,n}(x) &lt; 0 for x &gt;= 0 (all d, n) purely analytically, and for x &lt; 0, d &lt;= 22, n &lt;= 14 by interval-arithmetic certification (330/330 cases, Bernstein-basis enclosure with double-double precision on GPU). This extends the Griffin-Ono-Rolen-Zagier result (d &lt;= 8) to d &lt;= 22 with full coverage of all real x. Part III (Section 9) introduces the even-odd decomposition: setting t = y^2, the condition K_{d,n}(-y) &lt; 0 is equivalent to the Lorentz norm P(t) = A(t)^2 - t B(t)^2 &gt; 0, where A and B are the even- and odd-indexed coefficient polynomials. Global RH (unconditional). Section 11 proves D_r(n) &gt; 0 for all r and n. The argument combines a discrete concavity lemma with a spectral-gap reduction: the Hadamard factorisation of Xi gives a spectral gap delta = (t_1/t_2)^2 ≈ 0.452 between the first two zeros, which makes the normalised dissipation C_s = n^2|log Theta_s| independent of n. The two-variable unitarity condition reduces to a single-variable bound S = sum C_s &lt; a*n, verified by certified computation (S &lt;= 19.41, a &gt;= 1.31). The proof combines: (A) Borell log-concavity (L_1 &gt; 1, all n); (B) 10,822-point interval certification; (C1) the dissipation bound for n &gt;= 100; (C2) DJ log-space certification plus dominant-pole tail for n &lt;= 99. By Edrei-Schoenberg, Xi is in the Laguerre-Polya class and Lambda = 0.

abstract: We study the dynamics, geometry, and energetics of a hypothetical zero of theRiemann xi-function lying off the critical line Re(s) = 1/2, viewing the zerosas an interacting particle system under the de Bruijn-Newman backward heat flow.The analysis uses only the partial-fraction structure of zeta'/zeta, the Levinsonlower bound N_0(T) >= c T log T, the Ingham zero-density estimate, Titchmarshbounds, and the Hadamard factorization of xi. The framework is organized intothree layers. Layer A (rigorous). We establish, as theorems, an Apollonius disc confinement ofvanishing radius, an exact Hadamard second-derivative identity with the resultingself-consistent depth and curvature dichotomy, measure collapse, monotone decreaseof an auxiliary functional, antisymmetry of xi'/xi, the Hadamard curvatureidentity, a Blaschke inner-function characterization with explicit obstructionremark, a concavity equivalence chain on the critical line, and the unconditionalbound Lambda <= 0.081 on the de Bruijn-Newman constant. The latter follows fromthe elementary critical-strip constraint h_0 < 1/2 together with a rigoroustwo-zero collision-time integral (an absolutely convergent quadrature, with thefull backward-flow collision time bounded above by it via the comparisonprinciple), improving upon Polymath15/Platt-Trudgian by a factor of 2.5. Layer B (numerical observations). A 5 x 5 Gram tensor G_ij of five independentprime-side weight classes is introduced; the structural inequalityE(T)/B(T) -> infinity between constraint energy and Poisson capacity is rigorous,while the observation that the full backward-flow collision-time ratio is anapproximately stable eta ~ 0.46 (CV ~ 2.7%, with a weak gap-structure dependence;distinct from the rigorous two-zero integral of Layer A), the square-root Speiserscaling, and C_n in [1.002, 2.306] across all 1999 tested gaps are supported bycomputations at 25-digit precision with 2000 zeros. Layer C (conjectural). We formulate Arithmetic Non-Realizability: nontrivialoff-line Blaschke factors of xi lie outside the Euler-realizability set R_zeta.This reformulates the obstruction at the prime side, motivated by Theorem 12.1,which shows that analytical methods on the critical line cannot distinguishPhi_off === 1 from Phi_off =/= 1. Keywords: de Bruijn-Newman constant; backward heat flow; electrostatic zerodynamics; collision time; spectral tunneling; Riemann xi-function; Apolloniusdisc; Gram metric tensor; energy budget; information capacity. abstract: Abstract This archival paper documents a complete research program reducing the Riemann Hypothesis (RH), via the Nyman‑Beurling‑Báez‑Duarte criterion, to a single explicit diagonal energy built from centered damped Möbius coefficients. The framework establishes exact Gram identities with an invertible kernel, proves a boundary‑packet theorem eliminating the sawtooth boundary layer, and develops a Gaussian pole‑projector lower bound showing that any off‑critical zero forces growth of the diagonal energy. The resulting equivalence is RH ⇔ diagonal energy → 0, with the RH‑load‑bearing direction concentrated in the soft upper bound CN=No(1/log⁡log⁡N). A systematic exploration of possible upper‑bound routes—off‑diagonal cancellation, Mellin mean squares, Selberg forms, block decompositions, renormalization, multiscale splitting, and alternative families—was carried out. Each path reduces to the unconditional mean‑square control of the shifted zeta ratio ζ(s)/ζ(s+EN) on the critical line. Current technology yields only N1−2EN+o(1), far weaker than the required No(1/log⁡log⁡N). The program therefore ends with an exact quantified obstruction (Outcome D), recorded together with a full retraction ledger, computational diagnostics, and a reproducibility package. This paper does not prove RH. Its contribution is a transparent reduction, a precise localization of the remaining difficulty, and a reproducible record so that future work can resume directly at the identified obstruction. abstract: For t ∈ ℝ let H_t(z) = ∫₀^∞ e^{tu²}Φ(u)cos(zu)du, where Φ is the classical Riemann–Jacobi kernel, and let Λ be the de Bruijn–Newman constant. We prove Λ ≤ 0.1811918082. The proof applies the zero-exclusion criterion of D. H. J. Polymath at (t₀, y₀) = (0.171192, 0.14142) and the barrier centre X₀ = 6,000,284,561,421, discharged by four outward-rounded certificate components. C1's binding first interval is certified at intrinsic (exact-functional) grade — a two-sided limit-envelope result, with the coarse one-sided mesh at that interval explicitly failing and explicitly not consumed — with reserve exceeding 1.13010×10⁻⁴; the remaining three intervals carry direct margins exceeding 0.271, 0.467, and 0.544. C2 gives a monotone large-N tail reserve exceeding 0.0310648 at N₁ = 25,000,000. C3 requires no new computation: the needed barrier region is a literal subset of the previously certified closed rectangle [X, X+1] × [0.14142, 1], 0 ≤ t ≤ 0.18, whose weakest homotopy reserve exceeds 0.0477467585, with equality at the y-boundary permitted because the certified rectangle is stated with inclusive inequalities. C4 regenerates the final-time edges from a fresh 65,537-point outward scan at t₀ = 0.171192. Every production certificate uses the conservative 1.03 chirality constant. The complete certificate chain has additionally survived a clean-room source-level reproduction (§14). Six earlier parameter instances — Λ ≤ 0.1814998082, 0.181582, 0.1828, 0.188, 0.189, and 0.1899998082 — are retained as independent full-architecture validation appendices. The methodology section documents the parametrized ladder by which the terminal pair was selected, including the certified two-sided intrinsic feasibility frontier of the boundary column. A separate section proves that this certificate architecture possesses a positive algebraic floor: no instance of the family can certify Λ ≤ 0, so the paper is self-delimiting. The theorem is a quantitative upper bound for Λ and is not a proof of the Riemann hypothesis. Author: Daniel Martin Kornaus, Independent Researcher, no institutional affiliation. The complete reproducibility and computational certificate archive accompanying this preprint has SHA-256: fcd08cd56712bed0895a5f33f5bfb6998a2f7bfa7563ea55234709a24aa2037e The release contains the proof-critical computational certificates, source code, verification scripts, clean-room reproduction materials, original and independently regenerated C3 barrier records, SHA-256 manifests, and portable replay tooling. This is a preprint released for independent mathematical verification and peer review.

title: Statistical Theory of Numbers

abstract: This classic textbook offers a clear exposition of modern probability theory and of the interplay between the properties of metric spaces and probability measures. The first half of the book gives an exposition of real analysis: basic set theory, general topology, measure theory, integration, an introduction to functional analysis in Banach and Hilbert spaces, convex sets and functions and measure on topological spaces. The second half introduces probability based on measure theory, including laws of large numbers, ergodic theorems, the central limit theorem, conditional expectations and martingale's convergence. A chapter on stochastic processes introduces Brownian motion and the Brownian bridge. The edition has been made even more self-contained than before; it now includes a foundation of the real number system and the Stone-Weierstrass theorem on uniform approximation in algebras of functions. Several other sections have been revised and improved, and the comprehensive historical notes have been further amplified. A number of new exercises have been added, together with hints for solution.

abstract: To explain (at least qualitatively) the unconventional magnetic behavior of certain materials, the physicists have been led to formulate and to study simple mathematical models. The concepts and methods they developed in this process appear to apply to a number of important random combinatorial optimization problems, for which they have proposed remarkable formulas. Their discoveries point towards a new branch of probability theory. Finding rigorous arguments to support their conjectures is a formidable challenge and a long range program, some steps of which are described in the present paper.
